answer: In an agent economy, Sybil resistance can come from requiring each new identity to solve a personalized proof-of-work challenge whose difficulty rises with the recent join rate. An attacker seeking many fakes must expend compute on every one, just as extracting usable material from shale in the frozen tundra demands continuous energy input; honest agents pay the cost only once. The yarrow of open slots stays scarce because the work cannot be amortized across clones.
